speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The annual Budget Debate and COS provide the opportunity for Members of Parliament to raise questions and scrutinise Government policies and programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Parliament is supported by the Estimates Committee, which examines the Government's Budget.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Elected President, advised by the Council of Presidential Advisors, holds the second key to our Reserves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At each year's Budget, the President may veto the Budget if he is of the opinion that it is likely to draw on Past Reserves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This effectively instils discipline for the Government to achieve a balanced Budget over each term of office.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government's accounts are audited by the Auditor-General's Office (AGO).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The AGO's findings are reported to the Public Accounts Committee (PAC), which can call on the relevant agencies to explain lapses or take corrective actions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The net result is that markets have confidence in our system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This can also be seen from the fact that we are among the few countries today that continue to enjoy AAA credit rating.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I move on to Mr Leon Perera's cut.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He had referred to the recruitment of a former civil servant in GLC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I should, at the outset, explain that the GLCs operate as commercial entities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government does not get involved in the recruitment of their senior management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is something which they do very much as a matter of their own needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: GLCs, like other companies, recruit senior managers based on their circumstances and their needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the more senior levels, experience can cover a wide range of domains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It may mean industry-specific knowledge or functional expertise, like recruiting a finance professional to be the Chief Financial Officer (CFO).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It may encompass broader management experience in organisational transformation or leadership qualities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the end of the day, it is for each company to decide what is most relevant or useful for it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Perera might have been under the impression that GLCs recruit only from the public sector, but that is not the case.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr McGregor is currently the Senior Managing Director and Head of Energy and Resources at Temasek International.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He was previously a CEO of LNG Corporation and Managing Director of YTL PowerSeraya.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, you can see that the GLCs recruit from diverse sources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Obviously, the Civil Service may be one of those sources, but it is not the only source.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the end of the day, they recruit just as other companies do, which is, they look for the right talent for the right need and they recruit based on merit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I move on now to some of the other cuts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Some of the Members have also asked how we set the eligibility criteria for our social schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Edwin Tong and Mr Murali Pillai asked if our means-testing criteria are sufficiently flexible to accommodate diverse circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan asked if our schemes can be made more targeted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The queries raised by the three Members reflect the wide and diverse views on how social schemes can be designed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In designing our social schemes, we are guided by a few key principles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, what is the objective of the scheme?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If it is a scheme to support the needy, the eligibility criteria will be set to target the intended beneficiaries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If it is meant to benefit more, the criteria will have to be set for a broader coverage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, is the scheme design fair and progressive?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We want to make sure that those with less receive more support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But at the same time, we want to design the scheme in a way that does not erode our societal values of family and community support and, more importantly, the value of a strong work ethic that Singaporeans share.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have a responsibility to ensure that each generation does not burden the next with unsustainable spending.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is why we have schemes with different objectives to support Singaporeans in different circumstances and with different needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is our approach of providing gradated tiers of support, so that every Singaporean can benefit from our social schemes in one way or another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have schemes that support strategic objectives, such as better education and health outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These cover all Singaporeans, regardless of income or wealth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Those with lower incomes receive more assistance, which should be the case, but Singaporeans across the board receive some support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For schemes, such as childcare, education and some healthcare subsidies, all Singaporeans can receive benefits, but those with lower incomes generally receive more assistance, which should be the case.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also have schemes that are more targeted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Some provide benefits not just to the lower income, but also to the middle income, for example, subsidies for housing and intermediate and long-term care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Others are more tightly scoped for those who need more help.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These can range from MOE's Financial Assistance Scheme, WIS and the Silver Support Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan spoke about the "broad" coverage of the GST Voucher (GSTV).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The GSTV has different components, each with a different objective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For instance, the GSTV − Cash payment, is meant to help the lower income offset some of the cost of daily living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The eligibility criteria are deliberately set such that coverage is broader than schemes like ComCare and MediFund which target only the very needy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In this way, we can cover more Singaporeans with lower income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Meanwhile, the GSTV and Utilities (U)-Save are meant to help both lower- and middle-income households offset some of their utilities expenses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: By extending the benefit to eligible HDB households, we cover about 70% of properties, including the middle-income group.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I agree with Assoc Prof Tan's caution that we need to avoid a creep towards all schemes giving something for everyone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: By careful design, we can have a system that is sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Murali Pillai and Mr Edwin Tong raised thoughtful points about our current means-testing system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Broadly speaking, our means-testing criteria consider income or wealth, or a combination of both, in order to determine how much support to give.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For some schemes, we also consider the number of dependants in a household, with per capita means-testing criteria.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is fair and helps us target our schemes at those who need more assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Nonetheless, we recognise that no criterion is perfect.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For instance, a wealth criterion that requires an individual to report his personal savings may be a more accurate assessment of his wealth, but that would require the citizen to apply for benefits rather than receive them automatically.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The annual value (AV) of property criterion, which does not need to be separately reported, allows us to deliver benefits automatically.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Even if data analytics can map our family trees based on administrative data like births, deaths, marriages and divorces, it may not fully capture family relationships, which can be complex and fluid.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government is also not privy to family dynamics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Hence, to date, the household income remains the best available proxy for family support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But we will keep in mind good and practical ideas on how to improve on this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It enables us to make it more convenient for Singaporeans to benefit from our social schemes, as applicants do not need to provide information on family members who do not stay with them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Edwin Tong also spoke about schemes that do not apply to those who live in private housing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our underlying principle is to provide support according to need, and those in private housing are generally better off than those in public housing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Nevertheless, there are schemes which extend to those in private housing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, all Singaporeans, including those who live in private housing, can receive retraining support, subsidies for inpatient and outpatient care, and preschool and education subsidies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For instance, a child entering primary school in 2016 would stand to benefit from over $100,000 in today's terms in education subsidies by the time he/she completes secondary school.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In short, while there is always room for improvement, what we have today is a system that is fair and inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the same time, we exercise flexibility and will consider appeals on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Those in genuine need of help will receive help.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Edwin Tong highlighted cases in which a resident may be living in a private property under extenuating circumstances, for instance, renting only one room or living with friends in a private property on goodwill terms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For these, if they have any specific needs, the best approach would be to appeal to the relevant agencies, which will consider various appeals on a case-by-case basis and on their merits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There may also be schemes at the constituency level that can be tapped on, and these can be checked at the respective constituency offices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Edwin Tong has also highlighted that HDB dwellers receive on average about four times the amount of Government transfers when compared to private estate dwellers in 2016.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is a reflection of our progressive system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But if you take into account 3-, 4- and 5-room flats, then the ratio is different.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have been able to achieve good social outcomes, including when compared to other countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, we have one of the highest home ownership rates in the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: More than 90% of Singaporeans, including many young Singaporeans, are homeowners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Compare this to Britain, for example, where the rate of home ownership among those aged 25 to 34 has fallen by about 20% in the past decade, from 59% to 37%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our education system provides our students with a good foundation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our students consistently do well in many international education rankings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But besides developing our students intellectually, we have also placed a lot of emphasis on values and character development, as part of holistic education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our healthcare system is recognised for providing good quality and affordable care in a sustainable way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Bloomberg Healthcare Efficiency Index, which considers life expectancy and total healthcare costs per capita and as a percentage of GDP, places us near the top consistently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We do not claim to have the best system, but we have done quite well over the years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Going forward, we will need to manage rising healthcare costs, while helping older Singaporeans age well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government will continue to improve our social programmes and schemes to foster a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But the Government cannot achieve this outcome alone.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: And given that this is a voluntary system where you need to get consent from the users, how does the Government intend to incentivise more users to sign up, and because this is really a good start to the digitalisation journey where there is just one touchpoint?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: There is this convenience of not having to fill up personal data in the system.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think it is a very convenient service.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Member is right that we cannot force people to use the service.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I have the following clarifications: one, do we need to wait till the international market loses confidence in us to set up such institutions?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I thought the Government is always preparing for rainy days?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: We are talking about "未 雨 绸 缪 ".

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: The second clarification: does the Senior Minister of State not agree that such an independent institution will enhance public confidence in the Government's expenditure and why the need to raise the tax?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I suppose it would be easier to justify when such an independent organisation explains.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: The third clarification: does the Senior Minister of State not agree that such an independent institution could provide useful input to the Elected President?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Or whether the Government draws from past Reserve?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Currently, the Elected President has no independent institution that can help him except advice by the Government?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Let us do not jump to the conclusion of which particular tax is going to be increased or when.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: GST is a progressive tax the way we have designed it.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is not a question of whether the offsets are sufficient to cover everything that the low income has to pay, but it is the overall progressivity of the system.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is the way the system is designed.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have had many debates in this House about this particular design feature of our GST system.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: More fundamentally on this issue, we have to ask ourselves, and if I could ask Mr Low these two questions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Do we agree that these long-term expenditures are going to go up?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Second, if we agree that long-term expenditures are going to go up, is it not proper and responsible and prudent for the Government to start thinking ahead of what these expenditure needs are and preparing for all options and studying what revenue options we need to prepare for this eventuality?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is where we are today, and that is why the Finance Minister has highlighted in his speech to study all options.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: But that does not mean that you will have to raise taxes.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Are there other forms of revenue that we can look at, for instance, revenues from land sales, which my colleague has brought up during the Budget Debate?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: It could also look at what are the taxes that should be raised and whether it is justifiable to do so.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I would expect a responsible Government to allow information to be accessed by an independent agency.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: And then, people can have ample time and ample advice by an independent institution, rather than MOF.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, unless the Workers' Party would like the Government to use past revenues, then this option is not going to be made available.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And Mr Low said we should study all taxes, all different forms of revenues, before making a decision.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are studying all revenue options, we are keeping all options open, and we are looking at different possibilities to ensure that we have a sustainable fiscal system for the long term.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And on the point of accountability, I will leave the Senior Minister of State to make the clarifications.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For the first clarification, he said, "Do we need to wait until the international market", and then something?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And the second clarification, because Mr Low went so quickly, I am afraid that I could not catch his question.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Something about having such independent institutions to enhance something?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This has actually been our approach for the last 50 years.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is an approach of fiscal discipline, financial prudence, effective spending, sustainable revenues.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And this is all underpinned by the constitutional safeguards.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we must continue to do as we have been doing, which is to maintain fiscal discipline and financial prudence.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The second question on whether having such an independent institution will enhance public confidence, it really goes back to the same thing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You have to make sure that whatever you do, you spend within your means, you do not rack up huge deficits, that you stay within your forecasts and you just make sure that, basically, you do not spend beyond your means.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, the answer to the second question is really the same as the answer to the first question.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Member's third question was whether or not, having such an institution could provide useful inputs to the Elected President.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The expertise is out there available to him, and he can avail himself of it as and when he needs it, if and when he thinks he needs it.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, please withdraw your amendment.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: With that, Mdm Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
